# Extension Member Patterns

Covers Dimension 4: Extending problem details with domain-specific fields.

See [citations.md](../citations.md) for full source details.

## RFC 9457 Extension Rules

Problem type definitions MAY extend the problem details object with additional
members [1]:

- Clients MUST ignore extensions they don't recognize [1]
- Names SHOULD start with a letter [1]
- Names SHOULD use ALPHA, DIGIT, and underscore only [1]
- Names SHOULD be three or more characters [1]
- Extensions are namespaced by the problem type [1]

## Common Extension Patterns

### 1. Validation Errors

RFC 9457 defines a validation error example with an `errors` array [1]:

```json
{
  "type": "https://example.net/validation-error",
  "title": "Your request is not valid.",
  "status": 422,
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "must be a positive integer",
      "pointer": "#/age"
    },
    {
      "detail": "must be 'green', 'red' or 'blue'",
      "pointer": "#/profile/color"
    }
  ]
}
```

Each error contains `detail` and `pointer` (JSON Pointer per RFC 6901 [27]) [1].

#### Variant: SmartBear Extended Validation

SmartBear extends the errors array with additional fields [11]:

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `detail` | Specific error description (max 4096 chars) |
| `pointer` | JSON Pointer to problematic request property |
| `parameter` | Query/path parameter name |
| `header` | Header name causing error |
| `code` | Provider-specific error context |

Example [11]:

```json
{
  "type": "https://problems-registry.smartbear.com/invalid-body-property-format",
  "status": 400,
  "errors": [
    {"detail": "Must be a positive integer", "pointer": "/quantity"}
  ]
}
```

#### Variant: Belgian Government Issues Array

BelgIF uses an `issues` array with different fields [15]:

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `in` | Location (body, query, path, header) |
| `name` | Field name |
| `value` | Provided value |
| `detail` | What went wrong |

#### Variant: RFC 7807 invalid-params

The original RFC 7807 used `invalid-params` with `name` and `reason` fields [26]:

```json
{
  "type": "https://example.net/validation-error",
  "title": "Your request is not valid.",
  "invalid-params": [
    {"name": "age", "reason": "must be a positive integer"}
  ]
}
```

### 2. Rate Limiting

Common extension fields for rate limiting [3] [25]:

```json
{
  "type": "https://example.com/rate-limited",
  "title": "Rate limit exceeded",
  "status": 429,
  "retryable": true,
  "retry_after": 30,
  "limit": 100,
  "remaining": 0,
  "resetAt": "2026-03-13T10:30:00Z"
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `retryable` | boolean | Whether retry is safe [3] |
| `retry_after` | integer | Seconds to wait [3] |
| `limit` | integer | Request quota [25] |
| `remaining` | integer | Requests left in window [25] |
| `resetAt` | string (ISO 8601) | Window reset time [25] |

### 3. Operational/Tracing Extensions

Cloudflare's production extensions [3]:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `error_code` | integer | Numeric error identifier [3] |
| `error_name` | string | Machine-readable error name [3] |
| `error_category` | string | Classification enum [3] |
| `retryable` | boolean | Retry viability [3] |
| `retry_after` | integer | Seconds to wait [3] |
| `owner_action_required` | boolean | Escalation flag [3] |
| `ray_id` | string | Request correlation ID [3] |
| `timestamp` | string | Event timestamp [3] |
| `zone` | string | Affected zone [3] |

Cloudflare defines 10 error categories: access_denied, rate_limit, dns, config,
tls, legal, worker, rewrite, snippet, unsupported [3].

### 4. Out-of-Credit (RFC 9457 Canonical Example)

The specification's own example [1]:

```json
{
  "type": "https://example.com/probs/out-of-credit",
  "title": "You do not have enough credit.",
  "detail": "Your current balance is 30, but that costs 50.",
  "instance": "/account/12345/msgs/abc",
  "balance": 30,
  "accounts": ["/account/12345", "/account/67890"]
}
```

Domain-specific fields: `balance` (numeric) and `accounts` (array of URIs) [1].

### 5. Error Code Taxonomy

A common pattern adds a `code` field for machine-readable error classification
beyond the type URI [10] [11]:

```json
{
  "type": "https://example.com/missing-param",
  "status": 400,
  "code": "400-09",
  "title": "Missing body property"
}
```

## Framework-Specific Serialization

| Framework | Extension Mechanism |
|-----------|-------------------|
| Spring Framework 6.0+ | `properties` Map unwrapped via ProblemDetailJacksonMixin [24] |
| ASP.NET Core | `Extensions` dictionary on ProblemDetails; ValidationProblemDetails has `errors` dict [20] |
| Quarkus | ConstraintViolationException → 422 with custom title [30] |
| FastAPI (fastapi-problem) | Keyword args on exception constructor [8] |
| FastAPI (fastapi-problem-details) | ProblemException with extra properties [7] |

### ASP.NET Core Compliance Note

ASP.NET Core's `ValidationProblemDetails` uses an `errors` field structured as
a dictionary with field names as keys and arrays of messages as values [20].
There is active discussion (GitHub issue #57714) about whether this structure
fully complies with RFC 9457's recommendation for the detail/pointer pattern [31].

## Gaps and Limitations

- No standardized structure for validation errors — RFC 9457 provides an example
  but does not mandate a specific format [1]
- No efforts to standardize common extension members (traceId, correlationId,
  retryAfter) through the IANA registry or industry conventions
- No standard discovery mechanism for available extensions per problem type
- JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) is recommended for validation errors, but alternative
  pointer formats (JSONPath, XPath) are also used in practice
